key_insight: BiVerify improves mathematical self-correction by requiring the same candidate solution to pass both backward constraint checks and forward reasoning checks.
engineering_relevance: Bidirectional verification offers a structured way to improve LLM math reliability by combining complementary checks with shared tools for precise computation.
method: Start with backward verification against the original problem constraints, then verify reasoning and objective completeness forward.
Dynamically switch direction, reset verification state, and revise candidates or verification flow when checks fail.
Use shared mathematical tools to separate logical reasoning from precise computation.
evidence_signal: Across five challenging math benchmarks and multiple DeepSeek, GPT, and Gemini models, BiVerify exceeds the strongest evaluated representative public baseline by 13.5 percentage points in average accuracy, with a 31.2-point margin on GPT.
watch_item: Repeated verification and revision may increase latency and computation cost; the abstract does not quantify this overhead or guarantee correctness.
paper_title: BiVerify: Closing the Loop Between Backward and Forward Verification for Mathematical Self-Correction
